key_insight: Synthetic biomedical data is useful, but it does not automatically predict real-world performance. The paper highlights the simulation-to-reality gap as the key barrier to turning virtual experiments into trustworthy biomedical insight.
problem_solved: This paper addresses the challenge of using synthetic datasets to train and evaluate biomedical machine learning models without overestimating how well they will work on real patient data.
method: Review and discussion of how synthetic data is used in biomedical ML pipelines.
Analysis of the simulation-to-reality gap: why models that perform well on synthetic data may fail in practice.
Focus on how to interpret synthetic experiments as tools for insight generation rather than direct proof of real-world performance.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, the paper is a reminder to validate synthetic-data-based results carefully before deployment. It helps teams design more realistic evaluation strategies and avoid misleading conclusions from overly idealized simulations.
visual_elements: A side-by-side pipeline diagram comparing synthetic training/testing versus real-world deployment.
A gap illustration showing performance dropping from simulation to reality.
An icon-based flowchart of the biomedical ML lifecycle: data generation, model training, validation, and clinical use.
A simple chart contrasting synthetic accuracy with real-world accuracy across datasets or tasks.
paper_title: From virtual experiments to biomedical insight with synthetic data
paper_authors: Margarida Victoriano, Milena Pavlović, Geir Kjetil Sandve, Hélder P. Oliveira, Artur Rocha
